1. a point, edge : proverbial, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἀκμῆς on the rasor's edge (see. ξυρόν); ἀμφιδέξιοι ἀκμαί the fingers of both hands, (Sophocles Tragicus); ποδοῖν ἀκμαί the toes, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. the highest point of anything, the bloom, flower, prime , of man's age, Lat. flos aetatis, ἀκμὴ ἥβης (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀκμὴ βίου (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν ἀκμῆι εἶναι = ἀκμάζειν, (Plato Philosophus); ἀκμὴν ἔχειν, of…

1. originally probably a thunderbolt , ἄκμων οὐρανόθεν κατιών (Hesiod) 
2. an anvil , (Homer), etc.: metaphorically, λόγχης ἄκμονες very anvils to bear blows, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

1. Lat. non castigatus, unchastised, undisciplined, unbridled, (Herdotus Historicus), attic, etc. 
2. licentious, intemperate , opposite to σώφρων, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—; so in adverb, ἀκολάστως ἔχειν (Plato Philosophus); comparative, ἀκολαστοτέρως ἔχειν πρός τι to be too intemperate in a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)
to sharpen, whet , μαχαίρας (Aristophanes Comicus); λόγχην (Xenophon Historicus):—;Mid., ἀκονᾶσθαι μαχαίρας to sharpen their swords, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

1. to hurl a javelin , τινός at one, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπί τινι (Iliad by Homer):—;the weapon is put in dative, ἀκόντισε δουρί darted with his spear, (Iliad by Homer); also in accusative, ἀκόντισαν ὀξέα δοῦρα darted their spears, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. with accusative pers. to hit with a javelin , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; Pass. to be so hit or wounded , (Euripides) 
3. to shoot forth rays , of the moon,…

1. without order, disorderly , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;in (Homer) of Thersites' words, disorderly :—; adverb -μως, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. κόσμος ἄκοσμος, a world that is no world , [variant datesAnthology Palantina; also of an inappropriate ornament, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)
